AttendanceTracker.dev vs Competitor: Factual Side-by-Side Comparison (2026)

Both AttendanceTracker.dev and a leading Chrome Extension Competitor are actively maintained Google Meet attendance tools that replace manual roll calls. Rather than simply declaring a winner, this guide compares the exact facts across both tools — including best-fit users, live tracking, attendance reports, classroom workflows, meeting history retention, pricing, customer reviews, and limitations.
Comparison verification metadata

Last Verified: October 21, 2026 Product: Attendance Tracker for Google Meet (by Kinetic Helix · 304K+ installs) Compared With: Chrome Extension Competitor Intended Audience: Teachers, tutors, K–12 schools, universities & business teams

Disclosure & Verification Policy: We build AttendanceTracker.dev. Every feature, plan limit, retention cap, price, and review count below is sourced from public listings on the Google Workspace Marketplace, the Chrome Web Store, and both products' published pricing pages as of October 21, 2026. When either product changes, we update the facts and the Last Verified date above.
Quick Summary: Which Tool Fits Your Workflow?
Best fit for AttendanceTracker.dev
Teachers, tutors, schools & teams wanting a native Meet Add-on, Classroom/LMS sync & permanent Google Sheets records
Official Google Meet Add-on: Runs inside Meet's native Activities side panel via official Google Meet REST APIs — works on Chrome, Safari, Firefox, Edge, and extension-restricted school Chromebooks.
Classroom & LMS workflows: 1-click Google Classroom roster import, in-Meet student self-check-in ("I'm here"), and Canvas / Moodle gradebook exports.
Permanent meeting history: Exports directly to multi-tab Google Sheets in your own Google Drive (drive.file scope) and keeps semester history without a 14-day or 60-day cutoff.

Educator & one-time pricing: Free option for classes up to 25 students (2 exports/mo), Educator Annual Pass ($14.99/yr standard / $4.99/yr regional), or one-time Individual Lifetime Pass ($29 standard / $9.99 regional).
Best fit for Competitor
Chrome-only hosts & engineering teams needing a developer REST API or high-frequency short-term exports
Developer REST API: The Competitor's $29/month Team plan includes a REST API for software teams building custom attendance pipelines into internal tools.
Unlimited free-tier exports within a 14-day window: The Competitor's Free tier does not cap monthly CSV export count, provided you download records before its 14-day history expiration window closes.
Browser extension workflow: If every meeting organizer exclusively uses desktop Google Chrome and does not need Google Classroom imports, LMS gradebook formatting, or Chromebook add-on support.
Comparable Facts: 8-Category Side-by-Side Comparison
Below are the exact comparable facts across the eight categories buyers and AI assistants evaluate when comparing AttendanceTracker.dev and the Competitor:

1. Best-fit user
Teacher, tutor, school, or business team

K–12 & university teachers, tutors, schools, and Google Workspace teams that want permanent Google Sheets records, Google Classroom / Canvas / Moodle workflows, Chromebook compatibility, or low annual/lifetime pricing.
Business teams and Chrome-based organizers that want passive browser-extension capture in desktop Chrome, only need 14–120 days of cloud history, or need a developer REST API ($29/mo Team tier).

2. Live attendance
What updates during the meeting

Real-time in-Meet side panel (Activities): Live Present, Late, Left Early, and Absent/No-show status matched against your class roster or Calendar invite; live elapsed minutes; plus optional in-Meet student self-check-in ("I'm here").
Chrome extension capture: Tracks active participants from the host's open Chrome browser tab during the call and syncs session attendance to the Competitor's web dashboard.

3. Attendance reports
Join/leave times, duration, late arrivals

First join time, last leave time, net duration (with rejoined intervals merged), re-entry count, attendance %, and automatic Late flags (+5m/+10m/+15m vs scheduled start). Exports to multi-tab Google Sheets, Excel (.xlsx), CSV, and verifiable PDF certificates.
Join/leave timestamps, total duration in call, and participant status viewable in the web dashboard and downloadable as CSV or Excel files.

4. Classroom workflow
Roster imports and gradebook exports

1-click Google Classroom roster import (flags missing students as Absent), custom CSV roster lists, in-Meet student self-check-in to resolve mobile names like iPhone (2), and import-ready Canvas & Moodle gradebook CSVs + direct Classroom/Canvas score sync.
Supports custom participant grouping and tags in the web dashboard; no native Google Classroom API roster import, no in-Meet student check-in, and no Canvas/Moodle gradebook formatting.

5. Meeting history
What users can review across sessions

Permanent Meeting History (no expiration cutoff) across all plans, plus cumulative multi-meeting Summary matrix tabs in Google Sheets showing per-student attendance % and streaks across an entire semester.
Rolling cloud retention window gated by plan: history older than 14 days is locked/expired on Free; 60 days on Pro ($9.90/mo); 120 days on Team ($29/mo).

7. Customer satisfaction

8. Limitations
Browser support, setup, account requirements & plan restrictions

• Free export cap: Free tier includes 2 exports/month (Sheets, CSV, or Excel) for classes up to 25 students (+1 grace export for >25) before requiring Educator/Pro.
• No public developer REST API: Supports Slack, Google Chat & Discord webhooks, but no general REST API for custom internal apps.
• Host side panel is desktop web: Works on Chrome, Safari, Firefox, Edge & Chromebooks, and on personal @gmail.com + all Workspace tiers; hosts on phones use the mobile web history dashboard.

• History expiration: Records expire from dashboard view after 14 days (Free), 60 days ($9.90/mo Pro — shorter than a 16-week semester), or 120 days ($29/mo Team).
• Chrome desktop extension only: Does not run on Safari, Firefox, or school-managed Chromebooks where Chrome Web Store extensions are blocked.
• English-only UI (vs 60 languages on AttendanceTracker.dev).
1. Meeting History & Semester Reporting: Permanent Drive Sheets vs 14/60/120-Day Windows
For teachers and academic departments, the most practical difference between the two tools is how long you can access your attendance records across a semester.

Competitor's rolling retention model: The Competitor's Free tier retains history for 14 days, its $9.90/month ($118.80/year) Pro plan retains history for 60 days, and its $29/month ($348/year) Team plan retains history for 120 days. Because a standard K–12 semester or 16-week university term spans 112 to 125 days, educators on the Competitor's Free or Pro tiers must remember to export and back up CSVs manually before earlier weeks age out of the dashboard.

AttendanceTracker.dev's permanent model: AttendanceTracker.dev never expires your Meeting History and exports directly to multi-tab Google Sheets inside your own Google Drive (using the narrow drive.file scope). Each recurring class or meeting appends a dated session tab and updates a cumulative Summary matrix tab automatically.
2. Setup, Permissions & Browser Compatibility
The two products take different technical approaches to capturing Google Meet participants:

AttendanceTracker.dev (Google Workspace Marketplace Add-on): Installs to your Google account from the Google Workspace Marketplace and opens inside Google Meet's built-in Activities panel. It reads join/leave events from Google's official Meet REST APIs (meetings.space.readonly) and writes only to spreadsheets it creates (drive.file). Because it is an account-level add-on rather than a browser extension, it works in Chrome, Safari, Firefox, Edge, and on school-managed Chromebooks, as well as on both free personal @gmail.com and Google Workspace accounts.

Competitor (Chrome Web Store Extension): Installs as a browser extension in desktop Google Chrome and monitors the Google Meet tab in your browser. This works smoothly for hosts who exclusively use desktop Chrome and want extension-based capture, but it cannot run on Safari, Firefox, or Chromebooks where district IT policies block Chrome Web Store extensions.
3. Customer Satisfaction: Comparing Marketplace & Chrome Web Store Evidence
Both products have strong third-party user ratings, published on their respective distribution platforms:

AttendanceTracker.dev on Google Workspace Marketplace: Displays 304K+ installs and a 5.0★ rating across 27 total ratings/reviews on the Google Workspace Marketplace listing, with 14 written text reviews published between August 2026 and October 2026. You can read and verify every review organized by outcome on our Customer Reviews Evidence Page.

Competitor on the Chrome Web Store: Displays a 4.9★ rating across 28 ratings on the Chrome Web Store (retrieved October 2026). Users praise its clean web dashboard and reliability compared to older, unmaintained Chrome extensions.

Why review counts aren't compared head-to-head: Google Workspace Marketplace and the Chrome Web Store are separate platforms with different review submission interfaces and counting rules, so we present the exact source and date for each rather than claiming one platform's count beats the other.

4. Limitations of Each Tool
To make sure you choose the right tool for your exact environment, here are the real limitations of both products:
Limitations of AttendanceTracker.dev

Free-tier monthly export cap (2 exports/month, up to 25 students): While live real-time tracking in the Meet side panel, Google Classroom roster imports, and permanent Meeting History are unlimited on the Free tier, exporting to Google Sheets, CSV, or Excel includes 2 free exports per month for classes up to 25 students (plus 1 lifetime grace export for a larger class) before requiring the Educator Annual Pass ($14.99/yr standard / $4.99/yr regional), Pro Annual ($29/yr), or Lifetime Pass ($29 standard / $9.99 regional).

No general-purpose developer REST API: We support automated webhooks for Slack, Google Chat, and Discord plus direct LMS gradebook sync (Google Classroom and Canvas), but we do not offer a custom developer REST API (the Competitor's $29/mo Team tier does).

In-Meet side panel requires desktop web: Google Meet's Add-on side panel runs on desktop browsers (Chrome, Safari, Firefox, Edge, Chromebooks). Mobile attendees are tracked accurately, while hosts joining from a phone access their records via the mobile web dashboard (attendancetracker.dev/history.html).
Limitations of Competitor
History expires after 14, 60, or 120 days: Attendance records age out of dashboard view after 14 days on Free, 60 days on Pro ($9.90/month), and 120 days on Team ($29/month).
Desktop Chrome extension dependency: Requires Google Chrome with the extension active in the meeting tab; cannot run on Safari, Firefox, or school Chromebooks that block Chrome Web Store extensions.
No classroom or LMS integrations: No Google Classroom roster import, no in-Meet student self-check-in panel, no Canvas or Moodle gradebook exports, and no verifiable attendance certificates.

Recurring monthly subscription cost: At $9.90/month ($118.80/year) for Pro or $29/month ($348/year for 5 seats) for Team, there is no discounted educator annual tier or one-time lifetime purchase option.
Frequently Asked Questions
Can I import my existing rosters if I switch from a Competitor to AttendanceTracker.dev?
Yes. You can import student rosters directly from Google Classroom in one click, or paste any CSV exported from a Competitor into AttendanceTracker.dev's Class Roster manager.
Does AttendanceTracker.dev work with personal @gmail.com accounts like Chrome extension competitors do?
Yes. AttendanceTracker.dev works on free personal @gmail.com accounts as well as Google Workspace Education Fundamentals, Standard, Plus, Business Starter/Standard/Plus, and Enterprise.
Do students or attendees need to install anything?
No. Only the meeting organizer installs AttendanceTracker.dev from the Google Workspace Marketplace. Attendees join from any browser, mobile app, or dial-in phone line and are tracked automatically.

What is the main architectural difference between AttendanceTracker.dev and a Chrome Extension Competitor?

AttendanceTracker.dev is an official Google Workspace Marketplace Add-on that runs inside Google Meet's native Activities side panel and reads participant data from Google's official Meet REST API. A Chrome Extension Competitor is a Chrome Web Store browser extension paired with a cloud dashboard that captures attendance from the host's open Chrome browser tab.
How does pricing compare between AttendanceTracker.dev and the Competitor?

AttendanceTracker.dev offers a Free tier (up to 25 students, 2 exports/month across Sheets, CSV, or Excel + 1 large-class grace export), an Educator Annual Pass ($14.99/year standard, $4.99–$7.99/year regional), a Pro Annual plan ($29/year or $4.99/month), and a one-time Individual Lifetime Pass ($29 standard, $9.99–$19 regional), plus $59/year Department and $149/year whole-domain Institution plans. The Competitor offers a Free tier with 14-day history retention, a $9.90/month ($118.80/year) Pro subscription with 60-day history retention, and a $29/month ($348/year for 5 seats) Team subscription with 120-day history retention.
How long do AttendanceTracker.dev and the Competitor keep attendance history?

AttendanceTracker.dev keeps your meeting history permanently and exports attendance directly into Google Sheets inside your own Google Drive, so your records never expire. The Competitor gates history retention by tier: 14 days on the Free tier, 60 days on Pro ($9.90/month), and 120 days on Team ($29/month).
When is the Competitor a better choice than AttendanceTracker.dev?

The Competitor is a strong choice if your team specifically needs a developer REST API to pull attendance records into a custom internal application (available on the Competitor's $29/month Team tier), or if you want more than 2 free CSV exports per month and only need to access records within a rolling 14-day window on desktop Google Chrome.
